html:
The Middle East faces escalating tensions as the U.S. and Israel reportedly plan for a potential attack on Iran in early November, post-U.S. midterm elections, with Washington ordering diplomatic staff to leave Saudi Arabia. Trump stated the U.S. had inflicted significant damage on Iran and indicated new strikes are possible, while Iran revealed an "offensive" doctrine and warned of its readiness for the next war phase.

Middle East Security: The threat of a U.S.-Israel strike against Iran follows repeated Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, including King Fahd and Dammam airports, Aramco facilities, and the Saudi defense ministry, leading to multiple casualties and an Aramco staff evacuation in Dhahran. Explosions were also heard near the Strait of Hormuz, with reports of vessels hit. Egypt has pledged to defend Saudi territory, and Jordan condemned the Houthi attacks. Meanwhile, Egypt also declared a Turkey-Libya maritime deal "null and void," while Turkey, Qatar, Pakistan, and Indonesia formed a "Badr" deal to jointly produce weapons. Lebanon-Israel talks in the U.S. ended without a breakthrough amidst ongoing attacks.

Ukraine Conflict & Diplomacy: Russia pounded Kyiv with missiles just hours after reportedly agreeing to peace talks, while Moscow claimed to have downed over 800 Ukrainian drones. Amidst this, the U.S. and Ukraine face increasing strain over "mutual distrust" between Trump and Zelensky, even as the U.S. seeks to revive peace talks. Moscow is pushing for a summit with Trump and Xi Jinping to discuss ending the war, without Ukraine or the EU. Ukraine is exploring building its own sovereign satellite system with Finnish tech companies, following disruptions to Starlink, which Trump claims its owner Elon Musk has restored. Surveillance and "constant paranoia" are reported by Western diplomats working in wartime Moscow.

U.S. Domestic & Economic: Trump remains central in U.S. domestic news, being ordered to answer questions under oath in a BBC lawsuit. He also openly encouraged a "widely criticized campaign ad" from Republican opponent Vivek Ramaswamy featuring Amy Acton’s estranged mother. Corey Lewandowski, a former political adviser to Trump, is under criminal investigation for allegedly profiting off his government role. Economically, Trump stated Iran is attempting to drive up oil prices before midterm elections. In other news, Zuckerberg won a Meta deal to help him with a possible California billionaire tax, while Meta was also ordered to pay $25 billion in a New Mexico case over the Cambridge Analytica scandal.

International Security & Humanitarian: Hospitals in Sudan are being deliberately targeted by RSF fighters, a situation the UN human rights chief Volker Türk suggests may amount to war crimes. In Gaza, the death toll has reached 74,498 amid continued Israeli ceasefire breaches, with hospitals warning of an imminent shortage of generator oils threatening medical services. El Salvador's Nayib Bukele launched a military operation to rescue Salvadoran aviation technicians kidnapped by gangs in Haiti, deploying special forces after soldiers were ambushed. In France, Paris extended a curfew and major cities banned protests after riots, amidst scrutiny of the French police over brutality allegations, with German youth now planning similar mass protests.

Other Global Events: A magnitude 7 earthquake in China's Tibet killed at least 16 people and destroyed homes, while Super Typhoon Champi roars toward Taiwan and eastern China, leading to hundreds of flight cancellations across East Asia. On the health front, flu cases are rising on the U.S. west coast earlier than usual, prompting health experts to encourage vaccination. Brazil’s presidential runoff on Sunday holds high stakes for the Amazon rainforest and its communities. Separately, student-led rallies in Belgrade preceded Serbia's election, seeking to oust the party of Aleksandar Vucic.
